structured_output.what_is_happening: This is 'Agent.exe' (>_), a token whose pool was created directly on PumpSwap. The address has no 'pump' suffix, the launchpad is null and the pool is 11 minutes old. It is trading at a $17k market cap on $27.6k of liquidity. In that time it has done $356k of volume (about 13x its market cap), with 1,539 unique buyers against only 108 unique sellers, and the price is up 64%. A pump.fun token with the same name and ticker (92hj...pump) launched about 3 minutes earlier and is already at $105k market cap. Several other copies are dead at around $3k. This pool's LP is 100% unlocked, few wallets provide liquidity, the creator holds 0% and has closed out ('creator_close'), and GMGN flags 57 bundler wallets.

narrative.description: An AI-agent / 'agent.exe' terminal meme. The name looks tied to an X post (the GeckoTerminal link points to 0xsacramosa/status/...), so there was probably a tweet-driven launch race with many deployers copying it.
narrative.why_spreading: A tweet appears to have set off a sniping race across several same-name deployments. Attention is going to whichever contract traders see as the real one. That looks like the earlier pump.fun version with the higher market cap, not this one.

token_connection.why_this_token: Its only link to the story is the shared name and ticker. It was deployed about 3 minutes after the pump.fun version, straight onto a PumpSwap pool the deployer controls, with no socials or profile.
token_connection.competing_tokens: 92hjfSi5...pump (same name and ticker, $105k market cap, $208k volume in the last hour, launched earlier: likely the canonical one). There are also several dead copies, including GWFG..., 56aF...pump and BuNg...pump.

authenticity.evidence: Volume is about 13x market cap in 11 minutes. Unique buyers outnumber unique sellers about 14:1 (1,539 vs 108), which fits bot or airdrop-style buying spread across many wallets. GMGN counts 57 bundler wallets. The deployer seeded the pool and kept the LP unlocked. There is no smart-money or KOL participation.
authenticity.uncertainty: Copycat pools sometimes pick up real spillover buyers who confuse them with the original. Some of these buyers may be real people who aped the wrong contract.

structural_risks: 100% of the LP is unlocked and controlled by the deployer, so the liquidity can be pulled at any moment
The creator has already closed their position
It is a copycat of an earlier contract with more traction
The pool was created off the bonding curve, and the deployer platform is unknown

structured_output.counterargument: Buying is broad (1,500+ unique buyers), holders are spread out (top 10 hold 14%), and there is no dev bag. Momentum is still up +14% over 5 minutes. Spillover from the Agent.exe tweet could push even a copy to 2x from a $17k market cap, which takes only about $17k of net inflow. The creator's earlier token reached a $166k all-time-high market cap.

structured_output.thesis: This is a later-launched copycat of a tweet-driven Agent.exe token, sitting in a deployer-seeded PumpSwap pool with 100% unlocked LP. The volume looks bot-inflated, and the deployer can pull the liquidity whenever the pool fills. The canonical pump.fun version is already 6x its market cap and will soak up the real attention. It has a high rug probability and a low runner probability.
